issues.failure_explanation: In Theorem 4.1, the lower bound for the Lanczos iteration step m includes an extraneous factor of n in the numerator inside the logarithm (n K_{\rho_2}), and the definition of K_{\rho_2} uses an unbound variable \alpha instead of the optimal parameter \alpha^* defined by the scalar equation \alpha^* = 2\log \alpha^* + 2\log C + 1. In the derivation in Section 4, the factor of n cancels when bounding the quadrature error term by (\epsilon / \alpha) |\tr(f(A))| (since |\tr(f(A))| \ge n \log(\sqrt[n]{\kappa}/\lambda_{\max})), leaving the bound (4.1) and the objective constant C without any factor of n.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In Theorem 4.1, define K_{\rho_2} = \frac{4 \alpha^* M_{\rho_2}}{\rho_2^2 - \rho_2} using \alpha^*, and remove the factor of n from the numerator inside the logarithm for m, matching (4.1).
issues.overall_effect: As stated, Theorem 4.1 is ill-defined because \alpha in K_{\rho_2} is not specified, and the stated bound on m demands an unnecessary additive term \log(n)/(2\log\rho_2) Lanczos steps that contradicts the optimized MVM allocation problem solved in (4.3)-(4.4).
issues.title: Undefined parameter and extraneous factor of n in Theorem 4.1
issues.why_classification: The repair is a routine local correction that restores the exact formulas derived in equations (4.1)-(4.4) of Section 4 without altering any proofs, rates, or guarantees.
